verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS — Gate 3 passed subject to three mandatory pre-implementation corrections, all localised to WP-004's newly added second bind site and to one stale plan artifact. I independently re-derived ~35 load-bearing claims from the repo this pass (executed doorway preflight(); probed the engine MUTATIONS table; re-read sessions.py, writes.py, refusals.py, executions.py, manifests.py, runs.py, engine/manifest.py, engine/run.py, db.py, identity.py, setup.py, migrate.py, 0005, 0016, 0032, package.json, memory.md, git status). All five v1 blocking issues are genuinely addressed, not papered over: the B1 coverage gap is closed with a dataflow I re-derived hop by hop and confirmed (manifests.py:99 -> runs.py:128 -> engine/run.py:172 -> runs.py:332 -> runs.py:276 -> `value text` at 0005:83); WP-005's vacuous criterion is replaced by the only discriminating one; WP-008 is re-specified on a mechanism that exists in the repo (test_executions.py:418-424, verified verbatim); both hard-constraint-7 collisions are removed by deletion and by discriminator choice rather than by adding sequencing edges; and WP-009's type-checker criterion is replaced by a probe, with the absence of any type-checker config verified (no pyproject/setup.cfg/mypy.ini/pyrightconfig.json anywhere; package.json declares no devDependencies). The set also correctly REFUSED one v1 correction with evidence, and it was right to: the session deletes are at sessions.py:93 and :114, not 93 and :112 — I reproduced the grep, and 112 is the as_person line above the second delete. Refusing a reviewer correction on verified evidence is the behaviour this gate is supposed to produce. What blocks nothing but must be fixed first: WP-004's second site is specified with an exception contract that does not work as written, and it places its guard inside a function the repository has an explicit written decision NOT to tighten. Neither requires re-planning; both are two sentences of specification. Neither stops an implementer or makes a package unvalidatable — WP-004's own acceptance criterion (POST /runs dict value -> 400 rejected, demonstrated failing) catches the first at test time and bounds the second.

recommended_corrections: C1 — MANDATORY BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. WP-003 and WP-004 disagree about the shared helper's exception, and WP-004's version does not work. WP-003 says the helper raises 'the module's existing refusal exception' — that is `Missing`, defined at writes.py:99. WP-004 then says of manifests.py:99 that 'the helper's raising form is used directly here and no new error path is added'. Verified: `Missing` is caught in exactly one place, writes.py:681, inside writes.py's own answer wrapper; no other doorway module even names it. runs.py:129 catches only `manifests.Malformed`. So a dict-valued `value` would raise `Missing` out of manifest_from, pass runs.py's except clause untouched, and land in server.py:481's last-resort `except Exception` — a 500, which is the exact failure WP-004 exists to remove, and which contradicts its own acceptance criterion. Fix by specifying one of: (a) manifest_from catches the helper's exception and re-raises `Malformed`; or (b) the helper raises a neutral shape exception that each of the three call sites adapts (executions -> Answer 400, manifests -> Malformed). Either keeps hard constraint 3 intact. Do not leave 'used directly' standing.

C2 — MANDATORY BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. WP-004 places the guard inside `manifest_from`, which silently narrows a second endpoint, and the repository has a written decision against exactly that. runs.py:141-143 says verbatim: 'manifests.manifest_from is NOT tightened to match: POST /manifests/check is a pre-flight over anything a model might emit, and narrowing it here would silently change that endpoint.' It sits nine lines above the manifest_from call WP-004 cites and it was written about this very function. WP-004 neither quotes nor rebuts it, and states no acceptance criterion for POST /manifests/check. Resolve it in-package to the same standard WP-004 applied to its own KeyError question: either (a) guard `value` in runs.py after manifest_from returns, alongside the existing field-level 400 at runs.py:133-145, which leaves the pre-flight endpoint's contract untouched and needs no exception adaptation, so it also disposes of C1; or (b) tighten manifest_from deliberately, quote and overrule the comment, update it in the same change, and add a criterion stating what POST /manifests/check now does with a dict `value`. Note also that WP-004's caller enumeration is incomplete: manifest_from has three callers, and the third, documents.py:178, is missed. It does catch Malformed at :179 so tolerance holds, but it re-reads STORED manifests rather than request bodies, and the package should say so.

C3 — MANDATORY BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION, and cheap. The binding plan still contradicts the corrected packages. `integrated-revision-plan.json` still contains 'manifests.py:99 ... `value` reaches only dict members and string concatenation, never a psycopg parameter' and 'of which there is now exactly one'. The change log records that these 'must be corrected' but the file is unchanged. An implementer handed the plan and WP-004 gets opposite instructions about the same line. Apply both edits to the plan file itself.

C4 — recommended, low cost. memory.md is written by nine packages, all instructed to 'read the head at authoring time', while the set explicitly encourages parallelism (WP-002 in parallel with WP-001; WP-008 'can be scheduled to fill any gap'). Two packages authoring concurrently will both read S74 and both claim S75. Either name memory.md a serialised resource, or state that the S-number is assigned at merge rather than at authoring. This is the one shared-file contention the set does not address.

C5 — recommended, cosmetic but load-bearing for a set that trades on evidence. Drop the two Observed facts that have already drifted rather than re-dating them: memory.md's head is S74, not S67, and HEAD is d71ee7e, not 60ad1b6. The substantive claims behind both still hold (sessions.py remains modified and uncommitted, so EXT-1 stands), which is precisely why the volatile numbers should not be quoted at all.

C6 — recommended. WP-001 exempts the server.py row from EXT-1 on the grounds that it 'repairs committed state'. That is true of the staleness but not of the repair: server.py is also modified and uncommitted (verified, a 1-line diff), so the replacement pattern is quoted from a moving file too. The exposure is much smaller than the session rows' and the exemption is probably still right, but say so rather than implying server.py is settled.
